steps.prompt: A friend says $47 \times 38 = 1796$. Without working it out, can you tell if it is wrong?

cards.title: Two quick checks
cards.body: First, the size: estimate $47 \times 38 \approx 50 \times 40 = 2000$. Second, the last digit: only the last digits decide it, and $7 \times 8 = 56$, so the answer must end in $6$. $1796$ passes both checks (it is right).

steps.text: Estimate: $36 \approx 40$, and $40 \times 7 = 280$. $2520$ is about ten times too big.
Tom added an extra zero. The estimate caught it.

cards.title: Last digits of sums
cards.body: The last digit of a sum comes from the last digits: $47 + 38 + 29$ ends in the last digit of $7 + 8 + 9 = 24$, which is $4$.

prompts: Describe the two checks you can do on any multiplication answer.
